subject.title: feat: add lease-bound metadata to session spawns

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose the Agentic OS lease/session orchestration protocol as core Gateway API, or should core provide only a generic authorization/spawn seam for an owner-managed plugin or external integration?
rationale: The implementation introduces a new public, privileged session-orchestration contract and persistent state model; choosing its long-term ownership boundary is product and architecture policy, not a mechanical contributor follow-up.

options.title: Create a generic seam and externalize policy
options.body: Keep core limited to a documented generic authorization/spawn extension point and move Agentic OS-specific RPC names, metadata rules, and orchestration lifecycle to its owning integration.

options.title: Sponsor the core Gateway contract
options.body: Explicitly accept these RPCs and their compatibility, security, and persistence obligations as a maintained permanent core API, with owner assignment and upgrade guarantees.

recommendation.title: Create a generic seam and externalize policy
recommendation.body: Keep core limited to a documented generic authorization/spawn extension point and move Agentic OS-specific RPC names, metadata rules, and orchestration lifecycle to its owning integration.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the paired contract proposal and can clarify the integration requirements, though a core Gateway owner must make the final product decision.
